metadata.note: Q6b (3 marks): complete Rn-222 alpha decay equation (A, Z, element). Q6c(i) 'define half-life' is open — not auto-gradeable; excluded. Q6c(ii) (3 marks): calculate mass remaining after 4 half-lives.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q6b/c — Radon Alpha Decay and Half-Life
question.text:
Part (b): Radon-222 decays spontaneously by alpha particle emission to form Polonium (Po). Complete the nuclear equation:

\({}^{222}_{86}\text{Rn} \rightarrow {}^{A}_{Z}\text{Po} + {}^{4}_{2}\alpha\)

Find A (mass number), Z (atomic number), and name/symbol of the polonium isotope. (3 marks)

Part (c)(ii): A fresh sample of Radon-222, with half-life 3.8 days, has a mass of 240 g. Calculate the mass remaining after 15.2 days, to two significant figures. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q6b — Alpha decay:
A = 222 − 4 = 218
Z = 86 − 2 = 84
Element: Polonium-218 (\({}^{218}_{84}\text{Po}\))

Q6c(ii) — Half-life:
Number of half-lives: n = 15.2 ÷ 3.8 = 4
Mass remaining: m = 240 × (½)⁴ = 240 × 1/16 = 15 g

steps.label:
Alpha decay rules: Mass number A conserved: A(parent) = A(daughter) + 4  |  Atomic number Z conserved: Z(parent) = Z(daughter) + 2
Half-life: m = m₀ × (½)ⁿ  where  n = time ÷ half-life
Q6b — Complete the alpha decay equation for Rn-222. (3 marks)
Q6c(ii) — Calculate the mass of Rn-222 remaining after 15.2 days. (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Conservation of mass number: A(Rn) = A(Po) + A(alpha). So A(Po) = 222 − 4 = 218.
Conservation of atomic number: Z(Rn) = Z(Po) + Z(alpha). So Z(Po) = 86 − 2 = 84.

fields.label: Name or symbol of product: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Atomic number 84 = Polonium (Po). The product is Polonium-218.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The question gives the hint: the product IS Polonium. The isotope is Polonium-218 (²¹⁸₈₄Po).

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: (½)⁴ = ½ × ½ × ½ × ½ = 1/16 = 0.0625. After 4 half-lives, 1/16 of the original remains.
m = 240 × (1/16) = 240 ÷ 16 = 15 g. To two significant figures: 15 g.
